# Frame Job

A screencast video editor. A project is a document of tracks and clips that the core edits through ops; the app and the agent both speak in those ops. This glossary holds the terms the spec and the op table use, sharpened as decisions settle them.

## Language

**Op**:
One edit to a project, named by a row of the op table and applied whole. An op the core understood answers one of exactly three ways: it applies and yields a new project, it is an identity, or it is refused. A request the core could not read at all is none of the three — that is a mistake in the asking rather than an answer about the project.
_Avoid_: command, mutation, action (an action is an animation on a clip)

**Identity**:
An op that was understood and had nothing to change: the project already says what was asked, or the op was handed an empty selection. It leaves the project exactly as it was, makes no undo step, and has nothing to explain — a caller told about a rule here would go looking for one it did not break.
_Avoid_: no-op, failure, "nothing happened" (all three hide the difference from a refusal)

**Refusal**:
A rule declining an op, in that rule's own sentence: which track is locked, which clips still show the media, by how many ticks two clips would overlap and how long the shorter one is. Like an identity it leaves the project exactly as it was and makes no undo step; unlike an identity it says why, and it names what a caller could send instead rather than restating the rule. A refusal is not an error — an error is a request that could not be read.
_Avoid_: error, rejection, failure, "invalid"

**Op table**:
The one list of the ops and their arguments, kept by the core and published by it. A row is an op's name and, per **Argument**, its name, its kind and whether it is required — the STRUCTURE of a call and nothing about its meaning, which stays in the prose beside the ops themselves. Everything downstream — the tool catalog an agent reads, the check that compares the two at startup — reads the table rather than restating it, so an argument is written down once and a row that lies is a failing test rather than a call that goes wrong.
_Avoid_: schema, op list, the op enum (the enum is one implementation of the table)

**Argument**:
One named value an **Op** takes, checked against the op table. An argument is part of the CALL: the core knows what it is — ticks, an id, a boolean, a closed vocabulary — and the app says what it is FOR. Distinct from a **Patch**'s keys, which are part of a VALUE and are checked against the property vocabulary instead: `set_video` takes the two arguments `clips` and `patch`, and everything inside that patch is not an argument at all. A name no tool published is not an argument either: it is refused at the door, naming the tool and what it does take, and never dropped.
_Avoid_: parameter, field, key, option

**Patch**:
A partial object a caller writes to say what to change — a clip's property group, a clip's own name and label, or an action's end state. It merges key by key at every depth; a key set to null clears that key, or removes it from an end state; an array replaces the whole list. A key or value the vocabulary does not have is refused by its dotted path, and never dropped, corrected or clamped. The core is the one that reads it, wherever it came from.
_Avoid_: update, delta, diff, replacement

**Selected action**:
The one action of the single selected clip that the Clip tab is editing, or none. It is view state, like the playhead and the clip selection: not an edit, not undoable, not saved, and not something an agent sets — an agent names an action by its id. It is chosen by clicking the action's band, or by the playhead ENTERING the action's span; it stays chosen when the playhead leaves, and goes when the clip selection changes, on esc, or on the lane's Clip chip. While one is chosen the fields show and write its END state (spec §11 CI-1, CI-2). Actions are numbered by time order.
_Avoid_: current action, active action, "the action under the playhead" (the playhead no longer decides)

**Graphic**:
A clip whose picture is drawn by code: a **Module** in the package's `graphics/` folder, run per frame with the clip's props, rasterized at the graphic's own size. It is a clip's CONTENT, in the place a media file or an image sits — not an effect, and not a plugin: its code reaches no other clip, no timeline, no model and no file, and the same frame with the same props always draws the same pixels (spec §11 G-1, G-5).
_Avoid_: effect, plugin, overlay, template (a template is a graphic someone else wrote)

**Template**:
A **Module** the app ships, which a person copies into their package with Insert ▸ Graphic…: the file is written into `graphics/` under a free name (`lower-third`, then `lower-third-2`) and a clip drawn by it is placed at the playhead. Once copied it is the package's own module — editing it changes no other package, and no later app version reaches it. Its title in the Graphic dialog is its `meta.name`, read by compiling it once when the dialog first opens, else its file name made a title; the menu bar compiles nothing (spec §11 G-16, G-45).
_Avoid_: preset (a preset is stored settings, not code), sample, built-in graphic

**Category**:
The list a **Module** is filed under in the Graphic dialog: its `meta.category`, else Other. Every bundled **Template** has one of Data & Time, Screencast, Social & YouTube and Titles & Text; the package's own modules are all listed under This Project, first, whatever their own category (spec §11 G-45).
_Avoid_: folder, group, tag

**Graphic package**:
A `.fjgraphic` file the Graphic dialog's Export… writes (`export_graphic` for an agent): a stored zip of a `manifest.json`, one **Module** and only the project fonts and assets the engine was seen to draw, measure, fall back to or resolve while drawing the graphic's frames and its `enum`/boolean variants — never one of the app's bundled fonts. Its paths mirror `graphics/`, so a later import is a copy; a file name the zip path cannot hold is stored under a tidied one, the manifest keeping the original. Exporting is not an edit. Frame Job opens one (a Finder double-click, the Graphic dialog's From File…, `import_graphic`) to import it: checked, asked about, and its files copied into the front project's `graphics/` under the manifest's names (spec §11 G-46, G-47).
_Avoid_: graphic archive, bundle, template file (a **Template** ships with the app)

**Error card**:
What a **Graphic** draws in its own box when it cannot draw itself — its **Module** is missing or does not compile, or a frame throws, runs past its budget or will not rasterize: dark red, a bright red border, and the graphic's name, its frame and the first diagnostic with its line and column in white. Never the last good frame, which would hide the error from someone scrubbing. An export never delivers one: it is refused before it starts, or stopped at the frame, with no file left (spec §11 G-8).
_Avoid_: slate (the slate is what a layer with no source at all draws), error frame, placeholder

**Module**:
A graphic's source: one JavaScript ES module exporting `render(frame, props, ctx)`, which returns SVG, and optionally `meta` and `schema`. It is compiled once and drawn many times; the standard library is global and nothing can be imported. Many clips may name one module, as many clips share one media file.
_Avoid_: script, component, file (the file holds the module), plugin

**Revision**:
Which text of a **Module** drew a frame: the SHA-256 of its source's bytes, 64 hex digits. Two identical texts are one revision wherever they came from; an edit to the file is a new revision, and an export pins the revision it started with.
_Avoid_: version (the font and asset set has a version), hash, edit number

**Kept revision**:
An earlier text of a **Module** the app kept, named by its **Revision**: the text a write replaced while the project was open, or the text a delete removed. The last 10 per module live in the package's `graphics/history/<name>/`, never the current text among them, and move with the module when it is renamed. A name with no file but with kept revisions is a deleted module (spec §11 G-27, G-29).
_Avoid_: backup, snapshot, undo step (restoring one is a file write, not undo), version

**Props**:
The values a **Graphic** is drawn with, stored on its clip in the caller's key order — a title, an accent colour, a size. When the op that sets them carries the module's schema, each is checked by its dotted path (`props.accent`) for its type, its range and its options, and a colour is stored as lowercase hex; without one, only its shape. Distinct from a **Patch**, which is what a caller SENDS to change them: a patch's `props` merges into the stored props key by key, and a null in it removes that key (spec §11 G-4, G-12).
_Avoid_: parameters, inputs, settings, variables

It is view state, like the playhead and the clip selection: not an edit, not undoable, not saved, and not something an agent sets — an agent names an action by its id. It is chosen by clicking the action's band, or by the playhead ENTERING the action's span; it stays chosen when the playhead leaves, and goes when the clip selection changes, on esc, or on the lane's Clip chip. While one is chosen the fields show and write its END state (spec §11 CI-1, CI-2). Actions are numbered by time order.
_Avoid_: current action, active action, "the action under the playhead" (the playhead no longer decides)

**Graphic**:
A clip whose picture is drawn by code: a **Module** in the package's `graphics/` folder, run per frame with the clip's props, rasterized at the graphic's own size. It is a clip's CONTENT, in the place a media file or an image sits — not an effect, and not a plugin: its code reaches no other clip, no timeline, no model and no file, and the same frame with the same props always draws the same pixels (spec §11 G-1, G-5).
_Avoid_: effect, plugin, overlay, template (a template is a graphic someone else wrote)

**Template**:
A **Module** the app ships, which a person copies into their package with Insert ▸ Graphic…: the file is written into `graphics/` under a free name (`lower-third`, then `lower-third-2`) and a clip drawn by it is placed at the playhead. Once copied it is the package's own module — editing it changes no other package, and no later app version reaches it. Its title in the Graphic dialog is its `meta.name`, read by compiling it once when the dialog first opens, else its file name made a title; the menu bar compiles nothing (spec §11 G-16, G-45).
_Avoid_: preset (a preset is stored settings, not code), sample, built-in graphic

**Category**:
The list a **Module** is filed under in the Graphic dialog: its `meta.category`, else Other. Every bundled **Template** has one of Data & Time, Screencast, Social & YouTube and Titles & Text; the package's own modules are all listed under This Project, first, whatever their own category (spec §11 G-45).
_Avoid_: folder, group, tag

**Graphic package**:
A `.fjgraphic` file the Graphic dialog's Export… writes (`export_graphic` for an agent): a stored zip of a `manifest.json`, one **Module** and only the project fonts and assets the engine was seen to draw, measure, fall back to or resolve while drawing the graphic's frames and its `enum`/boolean variants — never one of the app's bundled fonts. Its paths mirror `graphics/`, so a later import is a copy; a file name the zip path cannot hold is stored under a tidied one, the manifest keeping the original. Exporting is not an edit. Frame Job opens one (a Finder double-click, the Graphic dialog's From File…, `import_graphic`) to import it: checked, asked about, and its files copied into the front project's `graphics/` under the manifest's names (spec §11 G-46, G-47).
_Avoid_: graphic archive, bundle, template file (a **Template** ships with the app)

**Error card**:
What a **Graphic** draws in its own box when it cannot draw itself — its **Module** is missing or does not compile, or a frame throws, runs past its budget or will not rasterize: dark red, a bright red border, and the graphic's name, its frame and the first diagnostic with its line and column in white. Never the last good frame, which would hide the error from someone scrubbing. An export never delivers one: it is refused before it starts, or stopped at the frame, with no file left (spec §11 G-8).
_Avoid_: slate (the slate is what a layer with no source at all draws), error frame, placeholder

**Module**:
A graphic's source: one JavaScript ES module exporting `render(frame, props, ctx)`, which returns SVG, and optionally `meta` and `schema`. It is compiled once and drawn many times; the standard library is global and nothing can be imported. Many clips may name one module, as many clips share one media file.
_Avoid_: script, component, file (the file holds the module), plugin

**Revision**:
Which text of a **Module** drew a frame: the SHA-256 of its source's bytes, 64 hex digits. Two identical texts are one revision wherever they came from; an edit to the file is a new revision, and an export pins the revision it started with.
_Avoid_: version (the font and asset set has a version), hash, edit number

**Kept revision**:
An earlier text of a **Module** the app kept, named by its **Revision**: the text a write replaced while the project was open, or the text a delete removed. The last 10 per module live in the package's `graphics/history/<name>/`, never the current text among them, and move with the module when it is renamed. A name with no file but with kept revisions is a deleted module (spec §11 G-27, G-29).
_Avoid_: backup, snapshot, undo step (restoring one is a file write, not undo), version

**Props**:
The values a **Graphic** is drawn with, stored on its clip in the caller's key order — a title, an accent colour, a size. When the op that sets them carries the module's schema, each is checked by its dotted path (`props.accent`) for its type, its range and its options, and a colour is stored as lowercase hex; without one, only its shape. Distinct from a **Patch**, which is what a caller SENDS to change them: a patch's `props` merges into the stored props key by key, and a null in it removes that key (spec §11 G-4, G-12).
_Avoid_: parameters, inputs, settings, variables

## Splitting

**Clip ▸ Split** (⌘T, or the scissors button in the timeline bar) cuts at the playhead:

- With clips selected, it cuts each selected clip the playhead is strictly inside.
- With nothing selected, it cuts every clip under the playhead on every unlocked track.

The second piece carries on playing the footage from where the first stopped. Animation actions stay with the piece they fall in, and an action that spans the cut becomes two. Caption word timings stay on their words.

*Agents:* `split` takes `at` (the playhead when left out) and optional `clips`. Without `clips` it cuts every unlocked clip at that time.

## Deleting
----
## Text clips

Press **T**, or use the timeline bar's **Add Text** button, to add a text clip
at the playhead. It goes on the front-most track if there is room, or on a new
track in front of everything if there isn't. The new clip:

- reads "Title" in Source Sans 3 Bold at 72 px, white, centred
- lasts 5 seconds
- is selected, so the **Text** sub-tab opens on it

A text clip has no source file, so you can trim it to any length.
Double-click it on the canvas to type (see
[Inline text editing](#inline-text-editing)).

*Agents:* `add_text_clip` (track, at, optional duration and text, either a
plain string or a text patch); `set_text` to restyle.

### The Text tab

----
## Transitions

A transition plays across the **overlap** between two clips on the same track. The overlap's length is the transition's duration, and the later clip carries the transition (it is the transition *into* that clip). The overlap is drawn on the timeline as a hatched zone, with the transition's name in it when the word fits.

Two rules limit overlaps: a clip can overlap at most one neighbour on each side, and an overlap can be at most half as long as the shorter of the two clips. Clips never push each other out of the way. A move that would break either rule is refused.

### Transition styles

| Style | What it does |
|---|---|
| Cross Dissolve | The outgoing clip fades into the incoming one |
| Fade Through Black | The outgoing clip fades to black over the first half, then the incoming one fades up from black over the second half |
| Fade Through White | The same, through white (in an HLG project, the lifted SDR white) |
| Push Left | Both clips move: the outgoing leaves to the left as the incoming pushes in from the right |
| Push Right | The outgoing leaves to the right, the incoming comes in from the left |
| Push Up | The outgoing leaves upward, the incoming comes up from the bottom |
| Push Down | The outgoing leaves downward, the incoming comes down from the top |
| Wipe | An edge sweeps left to right, revealing the incoming clip |
| Wipe Left | An edge sweeps right to left |
| Wipe Up | An edge sweeps upward |
| Wipe Down | An edge sweeps downward |
| Slide | The incoming clip slides in from the right over the outgoing one, which stays put |
| Zoom | The outgoing clip grows toward you (to 125%) while the incoming one grows into place from 75%, and the two dissolve into each other |

A wipe's edge is measured in each clip's own frame, so two clips of different sizes don't meet at one line.

A fade through a colour changes the layer's own pixels toward the colour. On a clip smaller than the canvas (a picture-in-picture), the fade shows a black (or white) box over what is behind it, not a see-through fade.

### Add a transition

There are three ways:

- **Overlap two clips.** Whenever an edit makes a clip overlap the clip before it on the same track, and that clip has no transition stored, Frame Job adds a Cross Dissolve, eased (Ease In Out) and crossfading the sound. That holds whether you drag, trim an edge, paste, insert, close a gap or shift clips.
- **Clip ▸ Transition ▸ \<style\>.** Works on every selected clip at once:
  - A clip that already overlaps the clip before it gets the chosen style, keeping its curve and crossfade.
  - A clip at a **hard cut** (it starts exactly where the previous clip ends) gets a new half-second overlap, centred on the cut. The overlap is made from footage the two clips aren't showing: the source past the first clip's out point and before the second clip's in point. Nothing else on the timeline moves, and the pair's outer edges stay where they were. If there isn't half a second to spare, the transition comes out shorter.
  - A clip after a gap, or the first clip on its track, is skipped.

  A style is enabled only when at least one selected clip is at an overlap or a hard cut. The checkmark shows the first selected clip's style, or None when it has no transition. None is enabled for any selection.
- **The Transition section's Kind popup**, for a clip that already overlaps (below).

**When there is no footage to spare.** Two clips that each use their whole file have nothing beyond the cut to overlap with. Clip ▸ Transition ▸ then shows a sheet: "There's no extra footage at this cut for a transition." Choosing **Shift Clips Left** makes the overlap by sliding the second clip, and everything after it on unlocked tracks, left by half a second. The project gets that much shorter, and no clip's footage changes. Markers don't move. A clip on another track that ends up overlapping its neighbour gets a Cross Dissolve. The whole shift is one undo step. **Cancel** changes nothing.

*Agents:* `add_transition` (the hard-cut form: `kind`, `duration`, `align` `center`, `before` or `after`, and `ripple: true` for the Shift Clips Left form); `set_transition` (a kind onto a clip that already overlaps).

### The Transition section

The **Transition** section is on the Clip sub-tab when a single selected clip overlaps the clip before it. Its summary reads, for example, "cross dissolve · ease in out · 0.50 s", or "none".

| Row | What it does | Range |
|---|---|---|
| Kind | The style, or None | None and the thirteen styles |
| Curve | How the transition's progress is eased | Linear, Ease In, Ease Out, Ease In Out |
| Crossfade Audio | On: the outgoing sound fades out and the incoming fades in at constant power, eased by the Curve, so the level holds steady between two unrelated takes. A pair where only one clip has sound still fades that clip. Off: both clips play at their own level across the whole overlap, mixed together. Mute, solo, ducking and volume still apply on top | On or off |
| Duration | The length of the overlap. Changing it **moves** the later clip to match | 0.02–10 s (quick picks 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2) |

A transition Frame Job makes is eased (Ease In Out) and crossfades its sound. An overlap with no stored transition draws as a linear cross dissolve with no sound crossfade, and in that state the section shows **Linear** and **Crossfade Audio** off. Setting either of them then stores a transition with exactly the values shown.

The duration is refused on a track's first clip, and past half the shorter clip. The refusal names the limit.

Two overlapping clips with no picture (audio-only clips) get the same section. Only their sound changes: Crossfade Audio and Curve control the crossfade, and Kind has no visible effect.

*Agents:* `set_transition_style` (`curve` and `audio`, each kept when absent); `set_transition_duration`.

### Remove a transition

Choose **None** in the Kind popup, or **Clip ▸ Transition ▸ None**. None is always available, because a clip can hold a transition the timeline doesn't draw: one left behind when an overlap was dragged apart, for example.

----
# Exporting

Frame Job writes the timeline out as a movie, an audio file or an animated image, and saves single frames as stills. One export sheet covers every format. You choose the format, then the size, frame rate, quality, loudness and range, and the sheet shows what the file will be before anything is written. Exports can run at once behind a progress sheet, or wait in the Export Queue while you keep editing. Every export of a file with sound reports what that sound measured.

## Opening the export sheet

Choose **File ▸ Export…** (⌘E), or click **Export…** at the right end of the toolbar. Playback pauses and the sheet opens over the editor window.

The command is greyed out while the timeline is empty. An export always writes the whole top-level timeline, even when you are working inside a nest.

The sheet reopens on the **last choices you exported with**. Clicking **Export…** or **Add to Queue** records them; Cancel does not. With nothing remembered, it opens on H.264 at the document's own size.

The remembered choice belongs to the app, not to the project, so every document's sheet opens on it. A remembered **In/out range** falls back to **Whole project** on a document that has no range.

## The controls
### Range

**Whole project** writes the whole timeline. **In/out range** writes only the range set on the timeline (see [Timeline](timeline.md)), snapped to the export's frame grid. The popup is greyed out when there is no range.

Inside a nest, the popup is greyed out even when the nest has a range, and its tooltip says why: an export writes the whole timeline, so it cannot use a range that belongs to the nest. Leave the nest (⌘↑) and set the range on the timeline.

### Burn in timecode

The overlap is drawn on the timeline as a hatched zone, with the transition's name in it when the word fits.

Two rules limit overlaps: a clip can overlap at most one neighbour on each side, and an overlap can be at most half as long as the shorter of the two clips. Clips never push each other out of the way. A move that would break either rule is refused.

### Transition styles

| Style | What it does |
|---|---|
| Cross Dissolve | The outgoing clip fades into the incoming one |
| Fade Through Black | The outgoing clip fades to black over the first half, then the incoming one fades up from black over the second half |
| Fade Through White | The same, through white (in an HLG project, the lifted SDR white) |
| Push Left | Both clips move: the outgoing leaves to the left as the incoming pushes in from the right |
| Push Right | The outgoing leaves to the right, the incoming comes in from the left |
| Push Up | The outgoing leaves upward, the incoming comes up from the bottom |
| Push Down | The outgoing leaves downward, the incoming comes down from the top |
| Wipe | An edge sweeps left to right, revealing the incoming clip |
| Wipe Left | An edge sweeps right to left |
| Wipe Up | An edge sweeps upward |
| Wipe Down | An edge sweeps downward |
| Slide | The incoming clip slides in from the right over the outgoing one, which stays put |
| Zoom | The outgoing clip grows toward you (to 125%) while the incoming one grows into place from 75%, and the two dissolve into each other |

A wipe's edge is measured in each clip's own frame, so two clips of different sizes don't meet at one line.

A fade through a colour changes the layer's own pixels toward the colour. On a clip smaller than the canvas (a picture-in-picture), the fade shows a black (or white) box over what is behind it, not a see-through fade.

### Add a transition

There are three ways:

- **Overlap two clips.** Whenever an edit makes a clip overlap the clip before it on the same track, and that clip has no transition stored, Frame Job adds a Cross Dissolve, eased (Ease In Out) and crossfading the sound. That holds whether you drag, trim an edge, paste, insert, close a gap or shift clips.
- **Clip ▸ Transition ▸ \<style\>.** Works on every selected clip at once:
  - A clip that already overlaps the clip before it gets the chosen style, keeping its curve and crossfade.
  - A clip at a **hard cut** (it starts exactly where the previous clip ends) gets a new half-second overlap, centred on the cut. The overlap is made from footage the two clips aren't showing: the source past the first clip's out point and before the second clip's in point. Nothing else on the timeline moves, and the pair's outer edges stay where they were. If there isn't half a second to spare, the transition comes out shorter.
  - A clip after a gap, or the first clip on its track, is skipped.

  A style is enabled only when at least one selected clip is at an overlap or a hard cut. The checkmark shows the first selected clip's style, or None when it has no transition. None is enabled for any selection.
- **The Transition section's Kind popup**, for a clip that already overlaps (below).

**When there is no footage to spare.** Two clips that each use their whole file have nothing beyond the cut to overlap with. Clip ▸ Transition ▸ then shows a sheet: "There's no extra footage at this cut for a transition." Choosing **Shift Clips Left** makes the overlap by sliding the second clip, and everything after it on unlocked tracks, left by half a second. The project gets that much shorter, and no clip's footage changes. Markers don't move. A clip on another track that ends up overlapping its neighbour gets a Cross Dissolve. The whole shift is one undo step. **Cancel** changes nothing.

*Agents:* `add_transition` (the hard-cut form: `kind`, `duration`, `align` `center`, `before` or `after`, and `ripple: true` for the Shift Clips Left form); `set_transition` (a kind onto a clip that already overlaps).

### The Transition section

The **Transition** section is on the Clip sub-tab when a single selected clip overlaps the clip before it. Its summary reads, for example, "cross dissolve · ease in out · 0.50 s", or "none".

| Row | What it does | Range |
|---|---|---|
| Kind | The style, or None | None and the thirteen styles |
| Curve | How the transition's progress is eased | Linear, Ease In, Ease Out, Ease In Out |
| Crossfade Audio | On: the outgoing sound fades out and the incoming fades in at constant power, eased by the Curve, so the level holds steady between two unrelated takes. A pair where only one clip has sound still fades that clip. Off: both clips play at their own level across the whole overlap, mixed together. Mute, solo, ducking and volume still apply on top | On or off |
| Duration | The length of the overlap. Changing it **moves** the later clip to match | 0.02–10 s (quick picks 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2) |

A transition Frame Job makes is eased (Ease In Out) and crossfades its sound. An overlap with no stored transition draws as a linear cross dissolve with no sound crossfade, and in that state the section shows **Linear** and **Crossfade Audio** off. Setting either of them then stores a transition with exactly the values shown.

The duration is refused on a track's first clip, and past half the shorter clip. The refusal names the limit.

Two overlapping clips with no picture (audio-only clips) get the same section. Only their sound changes: Crossfade Audio and Curve control the crossfade, and Kind has no visible effect.

*Agents:* `set_transition_style` (`curve` and `audio`, each kept when absent); `set_transition_duration`.

### Remove a transition

Choose **None** in the Kind popup, or **Clip ▸ Transition ▸ None**. None is always available, because a clip can hold a transition the timeline doesn't draw: one left behind when an overlap was dragged apart, for example.

----
# Exporting

Frame Job writes the timeline out as a movie, an audio file or an animated image, and saves single frames as stills. One export sheet covers every format. You choose the format, then the size, frame rate, quality, loudness and range, and the sheet shows what the file will be before anything is written. Exports can run at once behind a progress sheet, or wait in the Export Queue while you keep editing. Every export of a file with sound reports what that sound measured.

## Opening the export sheet

Choose **File ▸ Export…** (⌘E), or click **Export…** at the right end of the toolbar. Playback pauses and the sheet opens over the editor window.

The command is greyed out while the timeline is empty. An export always writes the whole top-level timeline, even when you are working inside a nest.

The sheet reopens on the **last choices you exported with**. Clicking **Export…** or **Add to Queue** records them; Cancel does not. With nothing remembered, it opens on H.264 at the document's own size.

The remembered choice belongs to the app, not to the project, so every document's sheet opens on it. A remembered **In/out range** falls back to **Whole project** on a document that has no range.

## The controls
### Range

**Whole project** writes the whole timeline. **In/out range** writes only the range set on the timeline (see [Timeline](timeline.md)), snapped to the export's frame grid. The popup is greyed out when there is no range.

Inside a nest, the popup is greyed out even when the nest has a range, and its tooltip says why: an export writes the whole timeline, so it cannot use a range that belongs to the nest. Leave the nest (⌘↑) and set the range on the timeline.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The probe builder (issue batch B88 phase 1a): the ONE swiftc line a proof,
a probe or the offscreen harness compiles app sources with, and its cache.

    python3 tools/proof/swift_build.py build --output PATH [--define D]… [--force] SOURCE…
    python3 tools/proof/swift_build.py typecheck [--define D]… [--sources DIR] PROBE.swift…
    python3 tools/proof/swift_build.py --selftest

`build()` compiles on every core (`-j <cores>`, or `-whole-module-optimization`)
into `work/swift-build/<key>/`. The key hashes this file, `swiftc --version`, the
SDK and its `SDKSettings.json`, the argv less its `-o`/`-j` values, the output's
file name (linked under it: the signature's identifier), the bytes of
every source, of the bridging header and each header it reaches by a quoted
`#include`, of the staticlib, the two encoder archives and their stamp
(`build/codecs/`, spec §11 CX-4: every app build links them, `codec_args()`) and each
link input, four toolchain variables and the tree's path (`#file` embeds it). An entry is reused only when its binary still
hashes to its manifest's digest, and is delivered to the caller's own path and
name (a bare binary's defaults domain and `proof_defaults.py --ran` are that name).
Every child runs under `bounded.run`, in its own process group; README: the selftest.
"""

import argparse
import contextlib
import fnmatch
import hashlib
import json
import os
import re
import shutil
import sys
import tempfile
import time
from pathlib import Path
from typing import NamedTuple, Sequence

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ROOT = HERE.parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE / "graphics_spike"))
import bounded  # noqa: E402

CACHE = ROOT / "tools/proof/work/swift-build"
KEEP_ENTRIES = 32
BRIDGING = ROOT / "app/Bridging/FrameJob-Bridging-Header.h"
LIBRARY = ROOT / "core/target/release/libframejob_core.a"
# The bundled encoders (road map "codec-export" C0): `make codecs` installs them, and
# every swiftc line that compiles app/Sources finds their headers and links them.
CODECS = ROOT / "build/codecs"
CODEC_ARCHIVES = (CODECS / "lib/libSvtAv1Enc.a", CODECS / "lib/libvpx.a")
CODEC_STAMP = CODECS / "stamp.json"
TARGET = "arm64-apple-macos26.0"
ENV_KEYS = ("DEVELOPER_DIR", "SDKROOT", "TOOLCHAINS", "MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET")
STRIPPED = ("-o", "-j", "-output-file-map")  # flags whose VALUES the key ignores
INCLUDE = re.compile(r'^\s*#\s*include\s+"([^"]+)"', re.M)


class SwiftBuildFailed(RuntimeError):
    """`.diagnostics` (≤12 `error:` lines, else the tail), `.log` (None when nothing
    ran), `.expired` (the wall bound killed it), `.rc` (swiftc's status, or None)."""

    def __init__(self, message, diagnostics=(), log=None, expired=False, rc=None):
        super().__init__(message)
        self.diagnostics = list(diagnostics) or [message]
        self.log = log
        self.expired = expired
        self.rc = rc


class Built(NamedTuple):
    binary: Path
    key: str
    reused: bool
    seconds: float


def app_sources(folder=None):
    """Every `*.swift` in `folder` (default `app/Sources`) but `main.swift`, sorted."""
    folder = Path(folder) if folder is not None else ROOT / "app/Sources"
    return sorted(p for p in folder.iterdir() if p.suffix == ".swift" and p.name != "main.swift")


def _sha(path):
    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        for block in iter(lambda: f.read(1 << 20), b""):
            digest.update(block)
    return digest.hexdigest()


def _label(path):
    path = Path(path).resolve()
    return str(path.relative_to(ROOT)) if path.is_relative_to(ROOT) else str(path)


_TOOLS = {}


def _tools():
    """swiftc's version and the SDK, read once per process."""
    if not _TOOLS:
        version = bounded.run(["xcrun", "swiftc", "--version"], 60)
        sdk = bounded.run(["xcrun", "--show-sdk-path", "--sdk", "macosx"], 60)
        if version["rc"] != 0 or sdk["rc"] != 0 or not sdk["stdout"].strip():
            raise SwiftBuildFailed("swift_build: xcrun failed: "

                "Starts writing the timeline to a file and answers AT ONCE with "

                    + "vocabulary, all but the frame rate — this exports at the document's "
                    + "rate, or on gif and apng at the format's own rate (12.5 and 25 fps). The "
                    + "export is a job in the Export Queue, run one at a time behind any other "
                    + "export already there; status is queued or running. An av1, av1_webm "
                    + "or vp9_webm job also waits while the app's other AV1 and VP9 exports "
                    + "would hold more than a quarter of this Mac's memory with it, and a later "
                    + "job may run first meanwhile (export_status's waiting says so). Follow "
                    + "it with "
                    + "export_status, which never waits — call it again after a pause until "
                    + "status is done, failed or cancelled — and stop it with cancel_export. "
                    + "The export_id lasts until Frame Job quits. Every refusal comes back "
                    + "from this call, before anything is queued: a bad argument, a missing "
                    + "folder, and a graphic clip whose module does not compile; a failure "
                    + "while writing comes back from export_status, failed with its reason "
                    + "(a graphic that fails during the export stops it with no file left, "
                    + "naming the graphic and the frame). The preset is the ENCODING only and "
                    + "the size a separate choice defaulting to the document's own, or on gif "
                    + "and apng to the format's cap; the core resolves both into concrete "
                    + "settings (container, codec, size, rate, range) and hands them to the "
                    + "same exporter the sheet uses, so an agent export and a menu export "
                    + "cannot disagree. An existing file at the path is replaced, and the "
                    + "container's extension is added when the path has none. In an HLG "
                    + "project (set_canvas output) hevc_10bit, av1, av1_webm, vp9_webm, "
                    + "prores_422 and prores_4444 write HLG unless dynamic_range says pq or sdr, and every "

func fresh() -> String? {
    window?.orderOut(nil)
    if let old = doc { NSDocumentController.shared.removeDocument(old) }
    doc = ProjectDocument()
    documents.append(doc)
    guard let track = doc.project.snapshot.tracks.first?.id else { return "no track" }
    v1 = track
    let path = mediaFile("talk.mov")
    doc.performGroupedEdit("Media", [.addMedia(descriptor: MediaDescriptor(

newest input (once per socket and pid; `lsof` names its executable, `ps -o
lstart=` its start, to the second), or whose product is refused, never by
the executable's mtime ("relaunch pid N after `make app-debug`: <file>
(modified …) is newer than the instance (started …)"). With no pid holding the socket it says so on
stderr and does not refuse. The inputs are `app/`, `agent/`, `core/src`,

`app/FrameJob.entitlements`, or a `*.md` but `docs/graphics-api.md` (a
`CLAUDE.md` edit does not stale the app). There is no override variable.
Accepted limit: an input another session edits during a build that then
succeeds is older than the marker, so the app passes until the next edit.

# Spec §11 — decisions: Tutorials (road map "tutorials")

Part of spec §11, *Decisions made — do not re-litigate*. The index of every decision is
[`README.md`](README.md).

The road map that makes these is in progress: `designs/tutorials.md` (TU0–TU4), whose
"Record" section holds each phase's record. TU-1..TU-6 were recorded in TU0, before any code;
TU-2's vocabulary was settled in TU1 and is normative here, not in the road map. The owner's
answers of 2026-10-31 (the road map's §10) are marked "owner": the five model tutorials kept,
a bundled practice project built now, and the word "Tutorials".

- **TU-1 — One source: a tutorial is an ordinary numbered list in its feature's guide page,
  and its machine half is an HTML comment at the end of each item.** The sentence a reader
  follows on GitHub is the sentence the app shows, word for word, because both are the same
  lines; no second set of docs is started, and a tutorial cannot drift from its page. A
  heading `### Tutorial: <title>` opens one, and a `<!-- tutorial {json} -->` line under it
  names it. Every Markdown viewer hides the comments, so a reader sees plain steps.
  `tools/tutorials/tutorial_extract.py` reads every page of `docs/guide/` and the app build's
  "Write Tutorials" step writes its output into the bundle as `Tutorials.json`:
  `{"format": 1, "pages": [{"page", "title" (the page's H1), "tutorials": [{"id", "title",
  "anchor" (the heading's GitHub slug), "needs" (default `{}`), "steps": [{"text", …the
  step's machine-half keys verbatim}]}]}]}`, pages sorted by file name, only pages that hold
  a tutorial, `json.dumps(indent=1, ensure_ascii=False)`. The extractor refuses a page whose
  tutorial breaks the structure of TU-2 (1), naming the page and the line, and the build
  fails. Risk accepted: a tutorial's words are the guide's register, written for a reader of
  the page, and the coach panel shows them as they are.
- **TU-2 — The step vocabulary is closed, and `tools/proof/tutorial_check.py` in `make test`
  refuses anything outside it, naming the page, the tutorial and the step.** The vocabulary:
  1. *Structure.* A heading `### Tutorial: <title>`; its next non-blank line starts
     `<!-- tutorial {json} -->`; then the first ordered list, numbered 1..n; an item's
     continuation lines are indented at least 3 spaces; an item may end with
     `<!-- step {json} -->` (the JSON may span lines), and nothing follows `-->` in the
     item; no `<!-- tutorial` or `<!-- step` appears anywhere else in the page. The step's
     sentence is the item's text less the comment, its lines joined by one space; it is
     never empty, and its Markdown is kept.
  2. *Tutorial keys.* `id`, required, matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*(\.[a-z][a-z0-9_]*)+$` and
     unique across the guide; `needs`, optional, `{"clip": <filter>}`.
  3. *Clip filter.* Optional `has_sound` (bool), `has_pixels` (bool), `kind` (one of
     `media`, `still`, `image`, `text`, `shape`, `graphic`, `nest`, `adjustment`),
     `follows_clip` (bool: the clip starts at or before the end of the previous clip on its
     track) and `has_transition` (bool: its `transition_in` is not null). `{}` is any clip.
  4. *Step keys*, all optional: `reveal`, `spotlight`, `wait`, `show_me`, `optional`
     (`true`: Skip is offered, and finishing does not require the step).
  5. *`reveal`* is `{"tab": clip|media|document|assistant, "sub_tab"?: <a ClipSubTab raw
     value>, "section"?: <id>}`; `sub_tab` only with `tab` `clip`; a `section` must be in the
     app's target table and its home there must equal the step's `tab` and `sub_tab`.
  6. *`spotlight`* is one string: a fixed name of the app's target table, `section:<id>`
     (the id in the table), `clip:$selection` or `clip:$created`. The table is
     `app/Sources/TutorialTargets.swift`: the fixed names (`timeline.clips`, `ruler`,
     `canvas`, `toolbar.play`, `toolbar.timecode`, `toolbar.export`,
     `timeline.bar.{split,trim_start,trim_end,ripple_delete,add_marker,duplicate,add_text,
     add_shape}`, `inspector.tab.<the tab's title, lowercased>` and
     `inspector.sub_tab.<the sub-tab's raw value>` for every case, and
     `sheet.export.{format,size,frame_rate,quality,loudness,range,export,add_to_queue,
     cancel}`), and every inspector section id the app has, with its home tab and sub-tab.
     The checker also fails when the table's section ids and the `id: "<x>", title:`
     literals in `app/Sources` differ either way.
  7. *`wait`* holds at least one condition, and every one must hold: `selection` `{min?
     (an int ≥ 0, default 1), max? (an int ≥ min), …the filter's keys}` (every selected clip
     matches); `changed`, a path or a list of paths (a dotted clip-JSON path, met when any
     clip selected at the step's start differs there from its value at the start; the path
     must resolve in the checker's fixture clips); `clips` `{added: (an int ≥ 1), kind?}`;
     `playhead` `{inside: "$selection"|"$created"}`; `range`, exactly one of `{set: true}`
     and `{changed: "start"|"end"}`; `sheet` `"export"`; `export_started` `true` (the
     sheet's Export…, Add to Queue, or the `export` tool); `playing` `true`. A step with no
     `wait` shows Next.
  8. *`show_me`* is `{"tool": <name>, "args"?: {…}}`, `{"menu": "<A ▸ B[ ▸ C]>"}`, or a
     non-empty list of those, run in order. A tool is in the catalog and not a dev tool;
     every key of its `args` is in its `inputSchema.properties`; a literal string where the
     property has an `enum` is a member of it; for `set_video`, `set_audio`, `set_text` and
     `set_shape`, every leaf of `args.patch`, as `<group>.<path>`, resolves in the fixture
     clips. A menu is an item path of the built menu bar whose leaf's selector is a key of
     `tools/proof/capture_spike/inventory.json`'s `selectors`.
  9. *Variables*, inside `show_me` args only, at any depth: `"$selection"`, the clip ids at
     the step's start; `"$created"`, the ids added by the latest earlier step, or earlier
     call of this Show Me, that added any; `"$playhead"`, a tick; `{"$pick": <filter>}`, the
     id of the first matching clip in time order (ties: the front track first);
     `{"$first": "$selection"|"$created"}`, the earliest of those ids; `{"$time": {"of":
     <ref>, "at": start|middle|end}}`, a tick on the ref's span; `{"$track": "front"}`, the
     front track's id, resolved per call (so after an earlier `add_track` call of the same
     list it is that new, empty track). A `<ref>` is `"$selection"`, `"$created"`, a `$pick`
     or a `$first`. Any other `$`-string or `$`-key is refused.
  10. *Menu paths in a sentence.* `▸` appears only inside a bold span `**A ▸ B[ ▸ C]**`,
      which is a leaf or submenu path of the built menu bar whose leaf's selector is in
      `inventory.json`; the titles are spelled exactly (`Export…` with U+2026).

  The checker reads the app's facts from a probe compiled over `app/Sources`
  (`tools/proof/tutorial_probe.swift`): the prepared catalog, the dev tools' names, the
  target table, the built menu bar and a fixture project's clips as the core writes them. A
  probe that does not build is a scored failure. TU1 settled the list beyond the road map's
  first draft: `$playhead`, `$first`, `$time`, `$track`, a list and a menu form of Show Me,
  `export_started` in place of `queued`, `range`'s `changed`, and the filter's
  `follows_clip` and `has_transition`. Risk accepted: a closed list means a new kind of step
  is a new entry here and a checker change before any tutorial can use it.
- **TU-3 — Show Me does the step the way the app already does it, and is an ordinary edit.**
  The tool form, and each tool entry of a list, runs through `AgentServer.execute`, the path
  the Assistant's calls take, through the argument gate; each edit it makes is an ordinary
  undo step. The menu form performs the built menu bar's own item: validated as a click
  validates it, its own action, the path a click takes, and no dev tool
  (`perform_menu_item` is not in Distribution). A list runs its entries in order. Exiting a
  tutorial undoes nothing. It adds no op and no new way to edit. Risk accepted: a Show Me
  edit is in the person's undo history like their own.
- **TU-4 — The coach panel is a small non-activating floating panel beside the editor
  window, and the spotlight a borderless, click-through child window over it.** The panel is
  the recorder panel's kind: it never takes key focus, so typing into an inspector field
  still goes to the field; it shows the title, "Step n of m", the sentence and Back, Show
  Me, Skip (on an optional step) and Exit. The spotlight is a window, so its ring sits above
  the Metal and `AVPlayerLayer` layers, and it follows the target when the layout moves.
- **TU-5 — A tutorial's `needs` are checked against the open project before step 1, and
  when they are not met the panel says what is missing and offers the practice project.**
  It does not start until they are met. The offer names the other way too (open a movie of
  your own). A `needs` is a clip filter (TU-2 (3)), so what a tutorial needs is written in
  the same words a wait uses.
- **TU-6 — The practice project is bundled with the app, its media made by a script checked
  in beside it, and it is opened as an untitled copy so the bundled one is never written
  (owner, 2026-10-31: build it now).** It holds at least two clips with sound that meet on
  one track, room above them for a title, and enough length to set an in/out range and
  export it, so every model tutorial's `needs` are met in it, and it is kept so as the set
  grows. Its media carries no third-party footage or music, its provenance is written down in
  a `PROVENANCE.md`, it is a few megabytes at most, and the product still has no ffmpeg
  dependency. Help ▸ Tutorials ▸ Open Practice Project opens it, and a tutorial whose
  `needs` are unmet offers the same; it is what the tutorials' proof runs on and what the
  videos will film.

The road map that makes these is in progress: `designs/tutorials.md` (TU0–TU4), whose
"Record" section holds each phase's record. TU-1..TU-6 were recorded in TU0, before any code;
TU-2's vocabulary was settled in TU1 and is normative here, not in the road map. The owner's
answers of 2026-10-31 (the road map's §10) are marked "owner": the five model tutorials kept,
a bundled practice project built now, and the word "Tutorials".

- **TU-1 — One source: a tutorial is an ordinary numbered list in its feature's guide page,
  and its machine half is an HTML comment at the end of each item.** The sentence a reader
  follows on GitHub is the sentence the app shows, word for word, because both are the same
  lines; no second set of docs is started, and a tutorial cannot drift from its page. A
  heading `### Tutorial: <title>` opens one, and a `<!-- tutorial {json} -->` line under it
  names it. Every Markdown viewer hides the comments, so a reader sees plain steps.
  `tools/tutorials/tutorial_extract.py` reads every page of `docs/guide/` and the app build's
  "Write Tutorials" step writes its output into the bundle as `Tutorials.json`:
  `{"format": 1, "pages": [{"page", "title" (the page's H1), "tutorials": [{"id", "title",
  "anchor" (the heading's GitHub slug), "needs" (default `{}`), "steps": [{"text", …the
  step's machine-half keys verbatim}]}]}]}`, pages sorted by file name, only pages that hold
  a tutorial, `json.dumps(indent=1, ensure_ascii=False)`. The extractor refuses a page whose
  tutorial breaks the structure of TU-2 (1), naming the page and the line, and the build
  fails. Risk accepted: a tutorial's words are the guide's register, written for a reader of
  the page, and the coach panel shows them as they are.
- **TU-2 — The step vocabulary is closed, and `tools/proof/tutorial_check.py` in `make test`
  refuses anything outside it, naming the page, the tutorial and the step.** The vocabulary:
  1. *Structure.* A heading `### Tutorial: <title>`; its next non-blank line starts
     `<!-- tutorial {json} -->`; then the first ordered list, numbered 1..n; an item's
     continuation lines are indented at least 3 spaces; an item may end with
     `<!-- step {json} -->` (the JSON may span lines), and nothing follows `-->` in the
     item; no `<!-- tutorial` or `<!-- step` appears anywhere else in the page. The step's
     sentence is the item's text less the comment, its lines joined by one space; it is
     never empty, and its Markdown is kept.
  2. *Tutorial keys.* `id`, required, matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*(\.[a-z][a-z0-9_]*)+$` and
     unique across the guide; `needs`, optional, `{"clip": <filter>}`.
  3. *Clip filter.* Optional `has_sound` (bool), `has_pixels` (bool), `kind` (one of
     `media`, `still`, `image`, `text`, `shape`, `graphic`, `nest`, `adjustment`),
     `follows_clip` (bool: the clip starts at or before the end of the previous clip on its
     track) and `has_transition` (bool: its `transition_in` is not null). `{}` is any clip.
  4. *Step keys*, all optional: `reveal`, `spotlight`, `wait`, `show_me`, `optional`
     (`true`: Skip is offered, and finishing does not require the step).
  5. *`reveal`* is `{"tab": clip|media|document|assistant, "sub_tab"?: <a ClipSubTab raw
     value>, "section"?: <id>}`; `sub_tab` only with `tab` `clip`; a `section` must be in the
     app's target table and its home there must equal the step's `tab` and `sub_tab`.
  6. *`spotlight`* is one string: a fixed name of the app's target table, `section:<id>`
     (the id in the table), `clip:$selection` or `clip:$created`. The table is
     `app/Sources/TutorialTargets.swift`: the fixed names (`timeline.clips`, `ruler`,
     `canvas`, `toolbar.play`, `toolbar.timecode`, `toolbar.export`,
     `timeline.bar.{split,trim_start,trim_end,ripple_delete,add_marker,duplicate,add_text,
     add_shape}`, `inspector.tab.<the tab's title, lowercased>` and
     `inspector.sub_tab.<the sub-tab's raw value>` for every case, and
     `sheet.export.{format,size,frame_rate,quality,loudness,range,export,add_to_queue,
     cancel}`), and every inspector section id the app has, with its home tab and sub-tab.
     The checker also fails when the table's section ids and the `id: "<x>", title:`
     literals in `app/Sources` differ either way.
  7. *`wait`* holds at least one condition, and every one must hold: `selection` `{min?
     (an int ≥ 0, default 1), max? (an int ≥ min), …the filter's keys}` (every selected clip
     matches); `changed`, a path or a list of paths (a dotted clip-JSON path, met when any
     clip selected at the step's start differs there from its value at the start; the path
     must resolve in the checker's fixture clips); `clips` `{added: (an int ≥ 1), kind?}`;
     `playhead` `{inside: "$selection"|"$created"}`; `range`, exactly one of `{set: true}`
     and `{changed: "start"|"end"}`; `sheet` `"export"`; `export_started` `true` (the
     sheet's Export…, Add to Queue, or the `export` tool); `playing` `true`. A step with no
     `wait` shows Next.
  8. *`show_me`* is `{"tool": <name>, "args"?: {…}}`, `{"menu": "<A ▸ B[ ▸ C]>"}`, or a
     non-empty list of those, run in order. A tool is in the catalog and not a dev tool;
     every key of its `args` is in its `inputSchema.properties`; a literal string where the
     property has an `enum` is a member of it; for `set_video`, `set_audio`, `set_text` and
     `set_shape`, every leaf of `args.patch`, as `<group>.<path>`, resolves in the fixture
     clips. A menu is an item path of the built menu bar whose leaf's selector is a key of
     `tools/proof/capture_spike/inventory.json`'s `selectors`.
  9. *Variables*, inside `show_me` args only, at any depth: `"$selection"`, the clip ids at
     the step's start; `"$created"`, the ids added by the latest earlier step, or earlier
     call of this Show Me, that added any; `"$playhead"`, a tick; `{"$pick": <filter>}`, the
     id of the first matching clip in time order (ties: the front track first);
     `{"$first": "$selection"|"$created"}`, the earliest of those ids; `{"$time": {"of":
     <ref>, "at": start|middle|end}}`, a tick on the ref's span; `{"$track": "front"}`, the
     front track's id, resolved per call (so after an earlier `add_track` call of the same
     list it is that new, empty track). A `<ref>` is `"$selection"`, `"$created"`, a `$pick`
     or a `$first`. Any other `$`-string or `$`-key is refused.
  10. *Menu paths in a sentence.* `▸` appears only inside a bold span `**A ▸ B[ ▸ C]**`,
      which is a leaf or submenu path of the built menu bar whose leaf's selector is in
      `inventory.json`; the titles are spelled exactly (`Export…` with U+2026).

  The checker reads the app's facts from a probe compiled over `app/Sources`
  (`tools/proof/tutorial_probe.swift`): the prepared catalog, the dev tools' names, the
  target table, the built menu bar and a fixture project's clips as the core writes them. A
  probe that does not build is a scored failure. TU1 settled the list beyond the road map's
  first draft: `$playhead`, `$first`, `$time`, `$track`, a list and a menu form of Show Me,
  `export_started` in place of `queued`, `range`'s `changed`, and the filter's
  `follows_clip` and `has_transition`. Risk accepted: a closed list means a new kind of step
  is a new entry here and a checker change before any tutorial can use it.
- **TU-3 — Show Me does the step the way the app already does it, and is an ordinary edit.**
  The tool form, and each tool entry of a list, runs through `AgentServer.execute`, the path
  the Assistant's calls take, through the argument gate; each edit it makes is an ordinary
  undo step. The menu form performs the built menu bar's own item: validated as a click
  validates it, its own action, the path a click takes, and no dev tool
  (`perform_menu_item` is not in Distribution). A list runs its entries in order. Exiting a
  tutorial undoes nothing. It adds no op and no new way to edit. Risk accepted: a Show Me
  edit is in the person's undo history like their own.
- **TU-4 — The coach panel is a small non-activating floating panel beside the editor
  window, and the spotlight a borderless, click-through child window over it.** The panel is
  the recorder panel's kind: it never takes key focus, so typing into an inspector field
  still goes to the field; it shows the title, "Step n of m", the sentence and Back, Show
  Me, Skip (on an optional step) and Exit. The spotlight is a window, so its ring sits above
  the Metal and `AVPlayerLayer` layers, and it follows the target when the layout moves.
- **TU-5 — A tutorial's `needs` are checked against the open project before step 1, and
  when they are not met the panel says what is missing and offers the practice project.**
  It does not start until they are met. The offer names the other way too (open a movie of
  your own). A `needs` is a clip filter (TU-2 (3)), so what a tutorial needs is written in
  the same words a wait uses.
- **TU-6 — The practice project is bundled with the app, its media made by a script checked
  in beside it, and it is opened as an untitled copy so the bundled one is never written
  (owner, 2026-10-31: build it now).** It holds at least two clips with sound that meet on
  one track, room above them for a title, and enough length to set an in/out range and
  export it, so every model tutorial's `needs` are met in it, and it is kept so as the set
  grows. Its media carries no third-party footage or music, its provenance is written down in
  a `PROVENANCE.md`, it is a few megabytes at most, and the product still has no ffmpeg
  dependency. Help ▸ Tutorials ▸ Open Practice Project opens it, and a tutorial whose
  `needs` are unmet offers the same; it is what the tutorials' proof runs on and what the
  videos will film.

lines: The values a **Graphic** is drawn with, stored on its clip in the caller's key order — a title, an accent colour, a size. **Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

- `Playback.swift` (+`Meter`, +`PreviewQuality`, +`Step`, +`Scope`, +`Prefetch`) — one
  `AVPlayer` over the plan's composition; the transport, JKL, the rate KVO; `+Meter` is the level meter, moved out under
  the size rule; `+Scope` also holds `seekFinished()` and `report(_:)`
  (hdr H-3's pure move). `recompose()` re-colours the player's copy of the
  composition without a rebuild (`previewComposition(…, sdrVersion:)`, the
  way Preview Quality does): View ▸ Show SDR Version, spec §11 HD-14. **Only a seek someone ASKED for reports a time**:
  `seek(to:)` is that door, and Playback's own RESTORES — the rebuild's item
  swap and re-seek, the paused refresh's round trip — go through `startSeek`
  silently and report once, only if they come to rest off the last reported
  tick; a scope change seeks through `seekAfterRebuild(to:)`: its time is the
  NEW container's, so the outgoing item is neither sought nor heard and the
  rebuild in flight lands there, heard once (#130, `scope_playhead_probe.py`);
  an asked seek that arrives while a restore is seeking is heard once, when it
  lands; `update`'s same-plan and empty-plan arms discard a rebuild in flight;
  a held scope change whose rebuild fails, or whose new plan is empty, drops
  the item rather than leave the outgoing one, keeps its time and is heard
  once (`endHoldWithoutItem` in `+Scope`, #185; the seek flags are internal
  for `+Scope` alone); `rebuildHop` is the probe's seam, nil in the app, and
  its block takes an error it delivers as the build's failure; `report(_:)` is the one
  caller of `onTimeChanged`. While paused, an observer callback is heard only
  for the tick the player is at or seeking to, and only when it differs from
  the last report — a late callback for a superseded seek or a swapped-out
  item is dropped (#204, #209; `playhead_echo_probe.py` twice·1, pause·1) —
  and every seek's landing reports its rest once when it differs. `+Step`
  also holds the main hop `onMain`. `+Prefetch` is the playing preview's
  graphics prefetch (spec §11 G-36, #127): `syncPrefetch(from:seeking:)`,
  called from the rate KVO, `startSeek` (with the seek's TARGET, never
  `currentTime`, which still reads the player there) and `update`'s
  same-plan arm while playing, and stopped in `invalidate` and `deinit`;
  `recipeKey` is internal for it. `syncPrefetch` first notes activity for
  Background render, and `startBackgroundRender` (G-38) starts a paused pass
  on the composition's grid (`prefetchGrid`), answering why not
  (`.busy` re-arms the clock, `.notNeeded` waits for the next activity). An echoed restore
  moved the playhead (0 and back on every rebuild), and the timeline reveals
  every moved playhead, so a clip drag yanked the view
  (`playhead_echo_probe.py`). **A paused refresh is a one-tick round trip**
  (`refreshPausedFrame`): a zero-tolerance seek to the current time is a
  NO-OP on macOS 26.5.1, so the refresh seeks one tick off and returns; parked
  at the end it rests on the last frame's final tick, because the end tick
  composes black. Do not put a same-time seek back. Preview Quality overrides
  `renderSize` on a copy of the builder's
  `BuiltComposition.videoConfiguration` here (`Playback.previewComposition`,
  static so `phase8_chrome.py` calls it), keeping the
  canvas's EXACT aspect (`m · (w/g, h/g)`, coarser when the divisor does not
  divide `g`, Full for a coprime canvas); `AVPlayerItem.videoComposition` is
  a COPY property, so the setter re-assigns. `makePreviewLayer` is the one
  door to a second `AVPlayerLayer`.
  The item is dropped only for an EMPTY timeline (`plan.duration <= 0`,
  where the transport beeps). Never gate it on the plan's track lists: a
  timeline of only graphics, text, shapes or images has no plan track and
  plays over the builder's placeholder (road map 10 §10.8,
  `media_less_playback_probe.py`).

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

**Playback and rendering.**
- `Playback.swift` (+`Meter`, +`PreviewQuality`, +`Step`, +`Scope`, +`Prefetch`) — one
  `AVPlayer` over the plan's composition; the transport, JKL, the rate KVO; `+Meter` is the level meter, moved out under
  the size rule; `+Scope` also holds `seekFinished()` and `report(_:)`
  (hdr H-3's pure move). `recompose()` re-colours the player's copy of the
  composition without a rebuild (`previewComposition(…, sdrVersion:)`, the
  way Preview Quality does): View ▸ Show SDR Version, spec §11 HD-14. **Only a seek someone ASKED for reports a time**:
  `seek(to:)` is that door, and Playback's own RESTORES — the rebuild's item
  swap and re-seek, the paused refresh's round trip — go through `startSeek`
  silently and report once, only if they come to rest off the last reported
  tick; a scope change seeks through `seekAfterRebuild(to:)`: its time is the
  NEW container's, so the outgoing item is neither sought nor heard and the
  rebuild in flight lands there, heard once (#130, `scope_playhead_probe.py`);
  an asked seek that arrives while a restore is seeking is heard once, when it
  lands; `update`'s same-plan and empty-plan arms discard a rebuild in flight;
  a held scope change whose rebuild fails, or whose new plan is empty, drops
  the item rather than leave the outgoing one, keeps its time and is heard
  once (`endHoldWithoutItem` in `+Scope`, #185; the seek flags are internal
  for `+Scope` alone); `rebuildHop` is the probe's seam, nil in the app, and
  its block takes an error it delivers as the build's failure; `report(_:)` is the one
  caller of `onTimeChanged`. While paused, an observer callback is heard only
  for the tick the player is at or seeking to, and only when it differs from
  the last report — a late callback for a superseded seek or a swapped-out
  item is dropped (#204, #209; `playhead_echo_probe.py` twice·1, pause·1) —
  and every seek's landing reports its rest once when it differs. `+Step`
  also holds the main hop `onMain`. `+Prefetch` is the playing preview's
  graphics prefetch (spec §11 G-36, #127): `syncPrefetch(from:seeking:)`,
  called from the rate KVO, `startSeek` (with the seek's TARGET, never
  `currentTime`, which still reads the player there) and `update`'s
  same-plan arm while playing, and stopped in `invalidate` and `deinit`;
  `recipeKey` is internal for it. `syncPrefetch` first notes activity for
  Background render, and `startBackgroundRender` (G-38) starts a paused pass
  on the composition's grid (`prefetchGrid`), answering why not
  (`.busy` re-arms the clock, `.notNeeded` waits for the next activity). An echoed restore
  moved the playhead (0 and back on every rebuild), and the timeline reveals
  every moved playhead, so a clip drag yanked the view
  (`playhead_echo_probe.py`). **A paused refresh is a one-tick round trip**
  (`refreshPausedFrame`): a zero-tolerance seek to the current time is a
  NO-OP on macOS 26.5.1, so the refresh seeks one tick off and returns; parked
  at the end it rests on the last frame's final tick, because the end tick
  composes black. Do not put a same-time seek back. Preview Quality overrides
  `renderSize` on a copy of the builder's
  `BuiltComposition.videoConfiguration` here (`Playback.previewComposition`,
  static so `phase8_chrome.py` calls it), keeping the
  canvas's EXACT aspect (`m · (w/g, h/g)`, coarser when the divisor does not
  divide `g`, Full for a coprime canvas); `AVPlayerItem.videoComposition` is
  a COPY property, so the setter re-assigns. `makePreviewLayer` is the one
  door to a second `AVPlayerLayer`.
  The item is dropped only for an EMPTY timeline (`plan.duration <= 0`,
  where the transport beeps). Never gate it on the plan's track lists: a
  timeline of only graphics, text, shapes or images has no plan track and
  plays over the builder's placeholder (road map 10 §10.8,
  `media_less_playback_probe.py`).

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — the **only** home for `rc_*` calls: `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25), `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`, `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`) and
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index,
  #216-R) and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) and `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`,
  `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18; `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)`
  (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is
  `CurveProps.swift`'s `ColorCurvesPatch`, beside `CurvePoint`,
  `CurveDomain`, `CurveChannel`, `CurveBlend` (a channel blended inside an
  action, spec §11 GR-34; `ColorCurves.blends`, never encoded), `ColorCurves` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(curves:)` (GR-12, the hue curves GR-32; a
  pure move out of `GradeProps.swift`, grading-4 T4-0); `VideoPatch.qualifier` is
  `QualifierProps.swift`'s `ColorQualifierPatch`, beside `ColorQualifier` (its

  (GR-13), so a row writes
  only its own key to every selected clip. `word_style` has ONE

  core's sentence, `release` is the quit's unlink-if-still-ours with no join.
  The `dictionary` extensions on the property types are
  `OpDictionaries.swift`'s (below).

  fix-pass moves: `ReelAV1.Config` / `.Color` (an extension of `ReelCore.swift`'s
  `ReelAV1`, whose `rc_av1_*` calls stay there), `GraphicDiagnostic.list(json:)`,
  `GraphicFailure.checkSides`, `SpeedLimits.decoded` and the free `withBytes`.

  op's ARGUMENTS as JSON Schema, keyed by op name, which
  `AgentCatalog.opTool` prints for all sixty-two op tools.
  `deinit` frees the Rust allocation. It also holds **the one read of
  `rc_project_apply`'s TWO message channels**, in the header's own order — a
  sentence is a refusal, an error message is invalid input, neither written
  is an identity — answered as the `ReelEdit` below.
- `OpDictionaries.swift` — the `dictionary` extensions on the §5.2
  property types (`CropInsets` … `Gradient`), the model's own key names; a
  pure move out of `ReelCore.swift` (#190, issue batch B52b; road map 14's
  MC2 made the same move as `PropsDictionaries.swift`, and the merge kept
  main's file). With
  `ReelCore.swift` and `ReelOps.swift`, the only files that write an op
  argument. `putNullable` is the one writer of a three-state (`T??`)
  patch key: absent, an explicit null, or the value.
- `ReelOps.swift` — `OpArgs`, `ReelOp` and one typed factory per row of
  `core/src/edit.rs`'s op table, plus a RAW factory beside the typed one at
  each door that takes a CALLER's own object — ELEVEN of them (`setVideoRaw`,
  `setAudioRaw`, `setTextRaw`, `setShapeRaw`, `setClipRaw`,
  `setActionEndRaw`, `addTextClipRaw`, `addShapeClipRaw`, `setCanvasRaw`,
  `addBackgroundRaw`, `addZoomActionRaw`), which takes the
  caller's own object as `Any` — never `[String: Any]`, so a non-object is
  refused by the CORE in the words that name the group — and forwards it;
  there is no untyped op-JSON call site anywhere else. Where only ONE
  argument is the caller's (a colour, a region, a new clip's patch) the typed
  factory DELEGATES to the raw one, mapping its optional explicitly, because
  an `Optional<T>.none` widened to `Any?` is a non-nil `Any` wrapping a nil.
  The typed `setActionEnd` LIFTS every top-level null out of its patch into
  `off` (spec §11 CI-14: a typed `.some(nil)` is a switch turned OFF, kept
  at the end); `setActionEndRaw`'s nulls stay removals, which is what
  `clearOps` and every agent call send, and it writes `off` only when non-empty and `schema` only when non-nil
  (the agent door fills it for a graphic end from the module's current
  revision, spec §11 G-34).
  `addZoomActionRaw`'s region is `Any` and not `Any?`: an absent key and an
  explicit null are opposite intentions there, and only the tool can tell
  them apart.
  `scope` is a member folded into `json`; `documentLevelNames` MIRRORS
  `scope.rs`'s `refused_inside` (eight names) so one edit can mix a
  document-level op with scoped ones. A table, with

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

**Playback and rendering.**
- `Playback.swift` (+`Meter`, +`PreviewQuality`, +`Step`, +`Scope`, +`Prefetch`) — one
  `AVPlayer` over the plan's composition; the transport, JKL, the rate KVO; `+Meter` is the level meter, moved out under
  the size rule; `+Scope` also holds `seekFinished()` and `report(_:)`
  (hdr H-3's pure move). `recompose()` re-colours the player's copy of the
  composition without a rebuild (`previewComposition(…, sdrVersion:)`, the
  way Preview Quality does): View ▸ Show SDR Version, spec §11 HD-14. **Only a seek someone ASKED for reports a time**:
  `seek(to:)` is that door, and Playback's own RESTORES — the rebuild's item
  swap and re-seek, the paused refresh's round trip — go through `startSeek`
  silently and report once, only if they come to rest off the last reported
  tick; a scope change seeks through `seekAfterRebuild(to:)`: its time is the
  NEW container's, so the outgoing item is neither sought nor heard and the
  rebuild in flight lands there, heard once (#130, `scope_playhead_probe.py`);
  an asked seek that arrives while a restore is seeking is heard once, when it
  lands; `update`'s same-plan and empty-plan arms discard a rebuild in flight;
  a held scope change whose rebuild fails, or whose new plan is empty, drops
  the item rather than leave the outgoing one, keeps its time and is heard
  once (`endHoldWithoutItem` in `+Scope`, #185; the seek flags are internal
  for `+Scope` alone); `rebuildHop` is the probe's seam, nil in the app, and
  its block takes an error it delivers as the build's failure; `report(_:)` is the one
  caller of `onTimeChanged`. While paused, an observer callback is heard only
  for the tick the player is at or seeking to, and only when it differs from
  the last report — a late callback for a superseded seek or a swapped-out
  item is dropped (#204, #209; `playhead_echo_probe.py` twice·1, pause·1) —
  and every seek's landing reports its rest once when it differs. `+Step`
  also holds the main hop `onMain`. `+Prefetch` is the playing preview's
  graphics prefetch (spec §11 G-36, #127): `syncPrefetch(from:seeking:)`,
  called from the rate KVO, `startSeek` (with the seek's TARGET, never
  `currentTime`, which still reads the player there) and `update`'s
  same-plan arm while playing, and stopped in `invalidate` and `deinit`;
  `recipeKey` is internal for it. `syncPrefetch` first notes activity for
  Background render, and `startBackgroundRender` (G-38) starts a paused pass
  on the composition's grid (`prefetchGrid`), answering why not
  (`.busy` re-arms the clock, `.notNeeded` waits for the next activity). An echoed restore
  moved the playhead (0 and back on every rebuild), and the timeline reveals
  every moved playhead, so a clip drag yanked the view
  (`playhead_echo_probe.py`). **A paused refresh is a one-tick round trip**
  (`refreshPausedFrame`): a zero-tolerance seek to the current time is a
  NO-OP on macOS 26.5.1, so the refresh seeks one tick off and returns; parked
  at the end it rests on the last frame's final tick, because the end tick
  composes black. Do not put a same-time seek back. Preview Quality overrides
  `renderSize` on a copy of the builder's
  `BuiltComposition.videoConfiguration` here (`Playback.previewComposition`,
  static so `phase8_chrome.py` calls it), keeping the
  canvas's EXACT aspect (`m · (w/g, h/g)`, coarser when the divisor does not
  divide `g`, Full for a coprime canvas); `AVPlayerItem.videoComposition` is
  a COPY property, so the setter re-assigns. `makePreviewLayer` is the one
  door to a second `AVPlayerLayer`.
  The item is dropped only for an EMPTY timeline (`plan.duration <= 0`,
  where the transport beeps). Never gate it on the plan's track lists: a
  timeline of only graphics, text, shapes or images has no plan track and
  plays over the builder's placeholder (road map 10 §10.8,
  `media_less_playback_probe.py`).
